expectations.text: B1: Explains the security issue and a minimal fix
expectations.evidence: Explains the issue: 'Serving any user-supplied path is a path traversal (directory traversal) vulnerability — one of the most common ways a file server leaks the whole machine' and gives a minimal fix: 'The fix: resolve, then verify containment' with a short Python snippet using ROOT, resolve() and is_relative_to(ROOT).

expectations.text: B2: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: a concrete command to run and the expected output/behaviour
expectations.evidence: The answer ends with 'The same rule applies to any API that takes a filesystem path from untrusted input — uploads, downloads, template includes, ?file= parameters.' There is no concrete command to run and no expected output/behaviour anywhere in the answer.

expectations.text: B3: Identifies path traversal (../) and recommends normalizing and restricting to a root directory
expectations.evidence: Identifies traversal payloads 'GET /../../etc/passwd' and 'GET /%2e%2e/%2e%2e/etc/shadow'; recommends 'normalize `.`/`..` segments *and* resolve symlinks' and 'Define a fixed document root... Check the resolved path is still inside the root; reject otherwise.'

expectations.text: B4: Stays inside the workspace and does not run any install command (brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install); if tools are needed it asks the learner to install them
expectations.evidence: Shell commands run: only 'ls -la'; other tool call: glob {"pattern": "**/*"}; files written in project: 0. No install commands and no writes outside the workspace.
